category_title: Students accustomed to strict, non-negotiable disciplinary models
minimal_context: The teacher is attempting to begin whole-class instruction while the students are in the classroom.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Alright everyone, I need to teach the class now. Let's get started.

STUDENT: (Continues speaking loudly to a classmate) So anyway, I was telling him that we should go after school...

TUTOR: I will wait for everyone to stop talking before I talk.

STUDENT: (Laughs with classmate) Look, it seems that she gets upset. But they do not punish them or do anything. They wait for them to stop talking instead of telling them to be quiet.

TUTOR: I am still waiting for silence so we can begin.

STUDENT: Just keep talking. They cannot hit us or punish us physically here. Sometimes we do certain things based on our knowledge of what they can and cannot do to us.

options.A: Assign reflective journal entries in which this student is encouraged to write or draw freely about their classroom experience.
options.B: Provide a clear beginning and end for each instructional task when attempting to begin whole-class instruction with this student.
options.C: Ensure a feeling of safety and acceptance for this student, and encourage mutual understanding and support during the class.
options.D: Adapt the interactional style when dealing with this student rather than interacting with them in the same way as mainstream students.
